g01: Short visit. Spend a week or two participating in ordinary life. Most people can be charming for two weeks. Congratulations: you have established that they can be charming for two weeks. 😅 Long visit. Stay long enough for inconvenience and conflict to appear. Observe how the person responds when tired, corrected, attracted, disappointed, or bored. Even a professional faker can sometimes perform for months; time gives you more evidence, not certainty.
g02: Long visit: stay long enough for the inconvenience and the conflicts to show up. Watch how the person reacts when they’re tired or corrected, attracted or disappointed, or just bored. Even a professional faker can sometimes keep it up for months! So time gets you more evidence, not certainty.
g03: Visitors, volunteers, workers, renters, and interns do not need full political membership to have rights. If a decision materially affects their compensation or access to shared resources, schedule, safety, housing, records, or discipline, they need clear terms, a way to be heard, and review. Egalitarianism that stops at the membership boundary can recreate a servant class between communes.
g04: Visitors, volunteers, workers, renters and interns don’t need full political membership to have rights. If a decision really affects their pay or their access to shared resources, they need clear terms and a way to be heard, and the decision should be open to review. The same goes for decisions that really affect their schedule, safety, housing, records or discipline. Equality that stops at the membership line? That can bring back a servant class of non-members moving between communes.
g05: “Outside” does not always mean the nation-state. My research initially leaned too far that way. The important thing is a competent layer that is not reviewing its own conduct: sometimes another community, a federation, a professional, an autonomous regional institution, a court, regulator, or emergency service. The Zapatistas are an important correction here: autonomous institutions can review local power without becoming the state. But autonomy is not permission to erase non-waivable individual rights, and it does not make outside jurisdiction disappear.
g06: “Outside” doesn’t always mean the nation-state. I’ll admit my research leaned too far that way at first. What matters is a competent layer that isn’t reviewing its own conduct. That could be another community, a federation or a professional. It could be an autonomous regional institution, or a court, a regulator or an emergency service. The Zapatistas are an important correction here: autonomous institutions can review local power without becoming the state. But autonomy doesn’t give anyone permission to erase individual rights that can’t be waived, and it doesn’t make outside jurisdiction disappear.
